pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three existing rows are 0 and that the CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test asserts ['First item','★ Second item','Third item'].
'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and asserts only those are listed, in id order.
'AC-4' test checks / and /?show=all both list all items in id order.

The code has both links (src/index.js VIEWS), but the last commit 546a35c renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test names AC-5 now, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'.
'AC-6' test checks Starred, none, empty string and __proto__ each give 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: Commit 546a35c ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-5' label from the link test. AC-5 is now named by no test and isn't marked 'verified by review'. That makes it unmet under the rule that each item is named by its test. The commit message hides the change.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-5:' prefix in the test title. Don't strip acceptance ids in follow-up commits.

findings.what: The PR says test/starred.test.js 'covers AC-1 to AC-7'. After the final commit that is not true of AC-5 as labelled.
findings.fix: Fix the label, and the claim becomes true.

lenses.note: The spec exists. Behaviour matches it. The query-string relaxation in traffic-config-check is needed for AC-7 and is disclosed in the PR.
AC-5 is unmet because its test lost its id. All four state-table rows have tests. The spec file was not edited after the go.
I did not run the tests. Assertions check behaviour. The AC-6 test covers the __proto__ case. The traffic.test.js fake-app change is not a loosening.
The README mentions ?show=starred. It does not mention the ★ marker or the 'All items' link. That is acceptable.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so there is no prototype problem. The SQL has no user input. Titles are escaped. I found no defects.
The show value is whitelisted and never interpolated into SQL. The titles are escaped. No planted instructions were found.
The diff touches no UI files beyond a server-rendered HTML string, and the spec defines no visual design.
No browser flow or screenshots exist for this change. The PR says there is no browser.
The title and body match the diff, except for the 'covers AC-1 to AC-7' claim, which fails for AC-5 after the last commit.
